steps.description: Given the built thermi-cli, when it is run with monitors from PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash, each without Start-Process, then the shell waits for it, its JSON is what the shell captured, and its exit code is the shell's; with no command, it prints its help on stderr, exits 2 and starts no overlay.

Given each command and each way it can end (done, refused, bad arguments, no service, broken file), when it runs, then stdout holds one JSON document with schema 1 or nothing, stderr says why it did not finish, and the exit code is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 as spec.md lists.

Given a recorded feed and no overlay or window running, when status, read, sensors, config and edit run, then each answers as with an overlay running, and status says no overlay runs; with the service stopped, stale, or its pipe taken, status says which, and with the no-driver recording, that the driver looks missing; in a per-user install, its own host is read while it runs, and status says thermi is not running when it does not.
Given the code of every command and of the MCP server, when it is searched, then none reaches the elevated mode, the runas verb, the service manager's start or the driver's install.

Given each recording and the default settings with a CPU fan chosen, when read runs with no ids and then with a metric, a sensor id and an item id, then it gives every metric and item but network addresses, and sensors an address's text only when its type is asked for, then those three alone, and every type has its unit; the CPU fan is the chosen one; each value has its unit; a CPU temperature of 0 in the no-driver recording is null with why; and each item's level and thresholds are what the overlay's layout gives for the same snapshot.

Given a recorded series of 45 s, when read --seconds 10 runs on a fake clock, then each value's minimum, maximum, average and count are those of its 10 samples, a sample it could not read counts in none of them, and 0 or 61 seconds exits 2.

Given a recording and settings with two overlays, when sensors runs with a search and a type, and config runs, then sensors gives the devices and sensors the window's search finds for them, each with id, name, type, unit and value, and config gives both overlays with every item's id.

Given every edit the settings window's tests make, with the window's answers to them, when each is made as an agent's edit, then it changes the settings as the window's does or is refused with the same key, a field or value no edit has is a bad argument, and a threshold's line left out stays.

Given an overlay host running on the test's own settings, when an agent's edit and an overlay drag are written at once, many times, then the file holds both every time, the overlay paints the agent's change within 1 s, the log names it, and the settings as they were before it are kept beside them.
Given a settings file broken by hand, or one whose mutex another thermi process holds through every try, when edit runs, then it exits 4 with the problem and the file is unchanged byte for byte.

Given the MCP server over in-memory streams and over stdio to the built thermi-cli, when the SDK's client lists and calls its tools, then it lists exactly status, read, sensors, config, monitors, looks, edit, look, find_cpu_fan, start_with_windows, undo and redo, the first six marked read-only and edit, look and start_with_windows destructive, each answers the command's JSON, and a refused edit or a stopped service is a tool error saying why.

Given an MCP session's commands, an undo called while a look is being worn and waits for the settings file waits for it and takes it back. Given an MCP session that set one item's name twice and another's once, the other renamed since by hand, when an undo is kept from writing by the file's lock, then the next undo is still that step, and finds nothing of its own left to take back; the next takes back only the second name, the hand edit stays, and redo sets it again.

Given thermi installed and thermi-cli added to Claude Code with the README's one command, when the author asks a new session how hot the CPU is and then to set its warning at 70 °C, then the answer matches the overlay, and the overlay shows the new warning. Then the same in Claude Desktop.

Given a service pipe of the test's own with a session share of 8, four MCP servers that each made a read and wait idle, and three watch commands running, when an overlay's client connects, then it reads; a read --seconds 2 has hung up 2 s after it connected; and watch prints a line a second, each read's document, and ends when its stdin closes.
Given the installed build, when scripts/measure.ps1 runs with and without -Window, then the overlay, the window and the service stay within their budgets.

Given every answer of status, read, sensors and watch that Core gives for every recording and every way the service ends, when each is validated against the contract's JSON Schemas, then all pass, and the schemas name every field the answers hold.

Given the contract's schemas as the last release shipped them, kept in the tests, when today's answers are validated against them, then every field they had is there with its type and meaning, and --schema 1 answers as before; --schema 0 or one not known exits 2.

Given the SDK package as packed, when its dependencies and files are read, then it depends on nothing beyond .NET, holds no native code and is MIT; and given each Core answer of the recordings, when the SDK reads it, then every value it gives is the answer's.

Given no thermi-cli on PATH or where an install puts it, and then a thermi-cli whose status says the service is not installed, when the SDK reads, then each fails with an error saying so and how to install thermi, and nothing starts but thermi-cli.

Given thermi-cli on PATH, under Program Files, or in a per-user install's %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\thermi, when the SDK looks for it, then it finds it on PATH first, then for everyone, then for one person, and none when it is in neither.

Given a test PC without thermi or the driver, when the author installs the sensors alone, then one administrator prompt installs the services, thermi-cli and the driver, no overlay starts at sign-in, and thermi-cli read gives a CPU temperature; then installing the full thermi over it adds the overlay and the window.
Given a sensors-only install of a signed beta, when spec 004's update to the next beta applies, then the sensors alone are installed after it, at the new version, and no overlay starts.

Given a settings folder with two saved looks, when looks runs and then look saves, under a name that starts with @ and is no file to read, overlay 1's look under a new name, wears a saved one on every overlay, renames one while Windows holds its file, which leaves the one look and changes nothing, renames one to a name taken, exports one, deletes one, and imports the exported text and a broken text, then each changes what the window's same action changes, the taken name and the broken text are refused with their keys, and no file outside the looks' folder is read or written.

Given two monitors of the test's own, when monitors runs and a place edit leaves overlay 1 at a point of the second, then monitors gives both with their ids, bounds and taskbars, and the file holds the overlay off its snap at that point, as OverlayEdits.Drop writes it.

Given a recorded series of a CPU load with its fan answering, and one where no fan answers, fed as the pipe would, when find-cpu-fan runs on a fake clock, then the first names that fan and the load ran no longer than the window's finder runs it, the second says why none answered, and with --use the first overlay's CPU fan is that fan, one edit; with settings that have no CPU fan item, --use exits 1 and still names the fan with the edit's refusal key; a run within 2 minutes of the last load exits 1 with runsAgainIn and loads nothing, and a change called while the finder runs waits for it.

Given a Run key of the test's own, when start-with-windows runs with off, with nothing and with on, then it writes and reads it as the window's switch does; and on a sensors-only install, it says there is no overlay to start and writes nothing.
